analysis:
release-swift.yml shrinks from the full pipeline to a thin wrapper (head lines ~160-172). The wrapper runs only on a tag or a workflow_dispatch with environment prod. It calls ./.github/workflows/release-provider.yml with environment: prod, passes through resume_run_id, resume_run_attempt, version_override and validation_only, and uses `secrets: inherit`. The concurrency group is now per run_id, so the shared `release-dev` serialization is gone from this file. The following base-side controls are removed from this file. Their equivalents are in a file not in this diff, so they cannot be confirmed present:
- `resolve-env` with `verify-source` against master, which ran before any credentials were used (base 161-205).
- Env-prefixed secret resolution that withheld prod secrets from dev and staging runs.
- Build and qualification jobs, plus the SDK 27 and exact-bytes checks (cmp of flat bin/ files against the app copies, CodeDirectory hash capture, full SHA-256 check).
- Entitlement checks (aps-environment=production, get-task-allow absent, keychain-access-groups).
- Notarization, stapling and spctl.
- Fan-helper signing requirement and layout assertions.
- Signed validation artifact retention and the publication stage/publish split with R2 staging.
- The older-macOS validation job.
The master-push dev release trigger and its path filters are not in the head wrapper; whether the new file reintroduces them is unknown. The next pass must read release-provider.yml (and the release-provider-build action) and confirm it preserves all of the above and the T-034 / A-011 registration invariants. Coverage is limited. needs_deeper_review is true.

findings.detail: The base release-swift.yml ran a `resolve-env` job first. It checked out `master` and ran `provider-release-resume.py verify-source` before any signing or publishing credential was used, so a candidate branch's policy could not authorize secrets. The head replaces all jobs with a call to `./.github/workflows/release-provider.yml`. That call hard-codes `environment: prod`, forwards `validation_only` and `version_override`, and uses `secrets: inherit`, which passes every repository secret (Apple signing cert, provisioning profile, PROD/DEV/STAGING R2 keys, release key). A local reusable workflow resolves at the triggering ref, and a `workflow_dispatch` on a non-master branch is allowed with `environment == 'prod'`. If release-provider.yml lacks an equivalent reviewed-source gate, a branch writer could obtain the A-005 release API key and Developer ID signing material, and register a build in A-011. That would weaken T-034 and T-013. The base also confined `validation_only` to dev; the head forwards it alongside `environment: prod`. The new file is not in this diff, so this cannot be confirmed. Fix: confirm release-provider.yml still verifies the source against master before any secret-consuming job, reject `validation_only` combined with prod, and replace `secrets: inherit` with an explicit allowlist of secrets.
findings.title: Release signing now delegates to a reusable workflow with `secrets: inherit` and a hard-coded prod environment; the source-trust gate is not visible
